title: The spherical perceptron with bi-orthogonally invariant disorder
note: Automated manuscript extraction. Mathematical correctness and proof completeness have not been independently checked.
abstract: We determine the limiting free energy of a spherical perceptron with a bounded continuous activation and a bi-orthogonally invariant disorder matrix. The singular values may have any compact limiting distribution, provided there are no outliers. We give an explicit variational formula for this limit.
sourceAbstract: We determine the limiting free energy of a spherical perceptron with a bounded continuous activation and a bi-orthogonally invariant disorder matrix. The singular values may have any compact limiting distribution, provided there are no outliers. We give an explicit variational formula for this limit.

statements.label: thm:angular
statements.text: For $\sum_jp_j\le1$ and $f\in C_b(\R)$, $P_M^f(a)$ converges in probability, uniformly on compact sets of $a\in[0,\infty)^h$, to a deterministic continuous function $P_p^f(a)$. Its explicit evaluation is given by \eqref{eq:angularformula} and \eqref{eq:pone} below. For $p<1$ and positive $a$, \eqref{eq:angularformula} holds for every sufficiently large fixed coefficient radius $\kappa$.

statements.name: Gaussian formula and global penalties
statements.label: thm:Gaussian
statements.text: For fixed $0<\theta<1$, fixed column counts $d_j$, and $n_j/M\to p_j>0$, let $D$ be bounded continuous, or the sum of a bounded continuous function and a nonpositive quadratic form. Then \begin{equation} \frac1M\log\calZ_{M,\theta}\left(\sum_{r=1}^M D(\xi_r)\right) \longrightarrow\Gauss_{\theta,p}(D) \end{equation} in probability and in expectation. More generally, let each $g_\ell$ be bounded continuous or a nonnegative quadratic form, let $\bar g=M^{-1}\sum_r g(\xi_r)$, and fix $d>0$ and $c\in\R^s$. The pressure for \[ H=\sum_rD(\xi_r)-Md\sum_{\ell=1}^s(\bar g_\ell-c_\ell)_+ \] converges in probability to \begin{equation} \min_{t\in[0,d]^s}\left\{t\cdot c+\Gauss_{\theta,p}(D-t\cdot g)\right\}. \end{equation} No restriction on $\sum_jp_j$ is needed.

statements.label: prop:aspect
statements.text: Theorem \ref{thm:main} remains valid for arbitrary deterministic dimensions with $M/N\to\alpha\in(0,\infty)$.

statements.name: Edge-interval control
statements.label: prop:edges
statements.text: In Theorem \ref{thm:main}, or Proposition \ref{prop:aspect}, let $s_-=\min\supp\nu$ and $s_+=\max\supp\nu$. The no-outlier assumption may be weakened to \begin{equation} \max_{r\le\min(M,N)}\operatorname{dist}(s_{N,r},[s_-,s_+])\longrightarrow0 \quad\hbox{in probability}. \end{equation} If $\alpha<1$, the interval may instead be $[0,s_+]$, using the macroscopic structural right null space at its lower endpoint. Forced left zeros do not provide such an endpoint.

statements.label: prop:activations
statements.text: Under either compact spectral condition above, the following extensions hold. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=*] \item If $f$ is continuous and $|f(z)|/(1+z^2)\to0$ as $|z|\to\infty$, the pressure converges in probability to the final bounded-cutoff limit of the main formula. Convergence in mean also holds, for example, if the spectra are uniformly bounded by a deterministic constant. \item If $f$ is bounded Borel and $\nu\ne\delta_0$, the pressure converges in probability and in mean. Its value is a final uniformly bounded continuous approximation limit, with approximation in Lebesgue measure on compact intervals as in the proof. \end{enumerate}
